label: number: the plural suffix -kal and when a bare noun already reads as plural
note: Chapter 93, and the old note's evidence was WRONG -- checked before it was used. It claimed -kal appeared inside four taught headwords, naming nirangal, maasangal, shareera-bhaagangal and kaalangal. Those four are FILE SLUGS, not headwords: ML-C11-nirangal carries the four colour words as its headword and ML-C16-kollavarsham-maasangal carries the twelve month names. A learner never reads a filename, so the suffix had been met zero times, not four, and this was not the free lesson the note advertised. A token sweep for the chillu-LL then found where it really was hiding: NINGAL (you, chapter 2) and NJANGAL (we, chapter 71) both end in -ngngal, and ML-CONCEPT-C02-RESPECT-BY-PLURAL-01 had already told the learner the respectful you IS a plural -- without ever isolating the ending that made it one. So the chapter reveals rather than introduces. It teaches -kal on a plain noun (kutti/kuttikal, kata/katakal), the -ngngal form a noun in anusvara takes in its place (pustakam/pustakangngal, maram/marangngal), and the label's second half -- a noun with a numeral in front needs no ending -- which the corpus was ALREADY doing correctly in three attested lines: ampathu rupa, nuru rupa, rantu mani. NO new vocabulary.
